what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Reader Skills sit on top of the story vault
sections.para: Markus Franz proposed Liquid Utility and six Reader Skills on 7 October 2026, using a bridge closure as his example, and said his idea connects with the story vault. Each skill is an operation the story graph already supports, each safeguard a graph property, and his article adds locality to the monetisation.

sections.label: Each Reader Skill is a question the graph can already answer
sections.line: Each Reader Skill is an operation on the graph
sections.para: Over a versioned story graph, Update is a diff rather than a summary, and Follow is that diff on a schedule, with freshness separating "could not check" from "nothing changed". Understand, Compare and Act are walks over claims; Relate joins the reader's data locally. Corrections are supersede edges, and anonymous sources are flagged at the node.

sections.label: The bridge, drawn
sections.line: One supersede edge is update, alert and correction
sections.para: The bridge becomes a graph: the council notice, diversion plan and a resident's photo are hashed evidence behind three claims, and the 9 October article is one projection. When the council moves the reopening on 21 October, one superseding claim serves as Update, Follow alert and correction. Relate tells the bus 42 reader about Station Road.

sections.label: What his article adds: the job, and the place
sections.line: Locality is where trust and willingness to pay concentrate
sections.para: Markus starts from the person's job, and that brings locality into focus: most of what touches daily life is local, and readers can verify local reporting themselves. Small payments from many people, a pound a month for bus-route changes or pence for a planning check, add up. The vault makes reliability verifiable.

sections.label: Local is where the facts are found, so let the money flow back to it
sections.line: Payments should flow back down to local sources
sections.para: In a story graph local contributors are nodes linked to the claims they support. As stories travel up to regional, national and international, each use could pay back down the chain in pence, shown as an illustrative split of one 10p use. Nothing on sgit.ai is wired to a payment rail yet.

sections.label: What a publisher could test, with both halves
sections.line: Start with one topic, vault, service and ledger
sections.para: Markus advises one maintained topic and one scoped service, measured on reach, utility, relationship and reciprocity. Three additions: keep the topic as a story vault from day one, record contributors in the graph so they can be paid, and publish the ledger. Reusable methods and a shared grammar make the second topic cheaper.

sections.label: Played out in full
sections.line: The bridge is now a full working simulation
sections.para: The bridge, followed to the end and its vault simulate three readers, three institutions and an agent using one local story graph from notice to reopening. Since version 0.2 it also counts costs, two years of long tail and trust. Markus ends with "Use it"; the addition is to pay those who found it out.

sections.label: Two infographics
sections.line: Two ChatGPT infographics are useful but drift from sources
sections.para: The infographic of this article follows it closely but uses its own bridge dates, says credit rather than pay, and misspells "informalton". The one of Markus's article gets the substance right but adds taglines, drops his qualifiers and omits his evidence on search. Places, dates and hashes in the bridge figure are illustrative.
